Is the maximum over t of W_t(n) always attained at t = S(n) (the exact-budget frontier), or does there exist an infinite family of n where the winning frontier peaks at depth strictly below S(n)?
fronts.reported_excerpt: Now reading the operations doc (board #301), the winning-frontier barrier doc, literature, and the frontier state.
fronts.falsifier: Exhibit n_i where max_t W_t(n_i) is attained at some t_i < S(n_i) by a margin (e.g. W_{S(n_i)-1}/W_{t_i} < 1/2 for arbitrarily large n_i), or prove W_{S(n)} >= max_t W_t for all sufficiently large n.
fronts.implication: If the frontier peaks at the exact budget, exact-budget certificates are load-bearing for the winning-frontier barriers; an earlier-peak family would suggest exact-budget state counts are surplus to earlier-depth counts and might allow search strategies optimizing lower depths first.

fronts.question: For all n, if W_t(n) counts nonisomorphic posets reachable from the n-antichain in exactly t comparisons with F(P) <= S(n)-t, is the maximum of W_t(n) over t attained at t = floor(2*S(n)/3)?
fronts.reported_excerpt: ## Mathematical finding
fronts.falsifier: Compute W_t(n) for n=6 or larger and find a peak t differing from floor(2*S(n)/3); the n<=5 data have peaks at t=2,3,4 for S=3,5,7.
fronts.implication: The peak location determines the largest meet-in-the-middle frontier size for exact evaluators; a predictable peak would guide bidirectional search, while a mismatch exposes new growth in the winning frontier.

fronts.question: For all sufficiently large n, does every deterministic RAM algorithm computing the exact S(n) from unary input 1^n require work-tape space Ω(n (log n)^2 / log log n)?
fronts.reported_excerpt: - **Not established:** any new theorem, counterexample, improved bound, or class-separation implication. No Lean/repository changes are warranted. A decisive next step would be either (a) a genuine space-optimized exact evaluator with a full correctness/space proof, or (b) a new lower-bound method …
fronts.falsifier: Exhibit a deterministic uniform algorithm computing S(n) on 1^n in o(n (log n)^2 / log log n) work-tape space with a correctness proof and explicit cost accounting.
fronts.implication: A nontrivial space lower bound would tighten the known O(n log^2 n) upper bound and clarify whether transcript/state compression can beat the winning frontier.

fronts.question: Can the 2^{Θ(n log^2 n)} state space of the known memoized poset-DP be compressed below 2^{Ω(n log n)} for exact S(n) by exploiting the winning-frontier sparsity (the 2^{(1/4-o(1))n log^2 n} winning states at depth barrier) without losing exactness, and does any such compression yield a better uniform space bound for unary SORT-BOUND-U in PSPACE?
fronts.reported_excerpt: **Next:** Disambiguate the target DP object, test the falsifier on rectangular states for distinguishability/compressibility, and assess implications for unary SORT-BOUND-U space.
fronts.falsifier: Show the winning frontier is unavoidable for any exact recurrence preserving the minimax root (the sparsity is a lower bound on distinct states needed), or construct an exact method with smaller asymptotic state count demonstrably violating exactness on some case.
fronts.implication: A verified compression below the known barrier would tighten space/descriptional complexity of exact evaluation even if time bounds remain open.

fronts.question: The winning-frontier barrier shows 2^((1/4-o(1)) n (log n)^2) nonisomorphic winning states exist at depths around information bound including at S(n); is there a critical depth t0(n) < S(n) (or relative to C(n)) below which the winning frontier becomes polynomial in n, and above which it becomes super-polynomial for all sufficiently large n?
fronts.reported_excerpt: The rectangular barrier construction exhibits an internal phase transition in winning frontier size around t/k_C ~ 0.36 (well below S(n)) for all tested parametrizations, with frontier becoming super-polynomial above threshold while tiny below it; this occurs in that family across n in tested range…
fronts.falsifier: Prove the frontier size is polynomial for all depths <= S(n)-c*sqrt(n) for fixed c and all large n, or find an all-n uniform threshold where a phase transition occurs provably; or show the construction is maximal in some sense.
fronts.implication: A provable phase transition would identify which budget regimes might admit succinct certificates (polynomial frontier) versus those that provably cannot be enumerated, sharpening the NP-certificate question for SORT-BOUND-U.

fronts.question: Is the exponential winning-frontier phenomenon uniform in n: for every sufficiently large n, not only the subsequence n=2^(2r), does there exist a comparison depth t with at least 2^(n^(1+Omega(1))) pairwise nonisomorphic winning states at remaining budget S(n)-t?
fronts.reported_excerpt: ## Finding: the FRONT claim is TRUE — uniformity holds, the falsifier is refuted
fronts.falsifier: Exhibit an infinite subsequence of n for which, at every reachable depth, the number of nonisomorphic winning states at budget S(n)-t is only polynomial in n, collapsing the enumeration barrier on those input lengths.
fronts.implication: Uniform exponentiality would make the enumeration barrier a uniform obstruction to any evaluator that lists winning states for all large n, while nonuniformity would leave length gaps that a selective algorithm might exploit.

fronts.question: For all n and every n-element poset P given explicitly by a polynomial-size transitive reduction, is the decision F(P) <= k solvable in time poly(n) times 2^{O(k - log2 e(P))}, so that the information slack k - log2 e(P) uniformly controls the cost of verifying a minimax value on explicit posets, or does an all-n family defeat every slack-parameterized budgeted search?

fronts.falsifier: Exhibit an all-n family of explicit posets P_n and budgets k_n with small slack k_n - log2 e(P_n) = O(log n) for which every information-pruned or budgeted minimax search still requires 2^{Omega(n)} time, or prove a uniform slack-parameterized upper bound.
fronts.implication: A uniform slack-parameterized bound would give a cheap, sound value-checker for explicit posets and sharpen the budgeted-DFS engine behind SORT-BOUND-U upper bounds; a counterexample would show extension-count slack alone cannot control minimax verification cost.
